features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal relevant technical education the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on experience architecting agent-based systems, especially with explicit boundaries, supervision, permissions, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic-systems experience is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned only vaguely, with little indication of direct design or implementation.
The letter shows clear experience building or working on agentic tooling, but with limited architectural detail.
The letter shows end-to-end design of Python agents paired with Go services, backends, or guardrails.
The letter shows especially mature agentic design, emphasizing constraints, permissions, auditability, or strategic infrastructure direction.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has real production experience deploying AI systems and addressing their reliability, evaluation, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful AI or LLM experience described.
Mentions AI features or interest without production detail.
States they shipped AI or LLM-backed functionality in production.
Shows production maturity by discussing evaluation, reliability, unpredictable inputs, failure modes, or trustworthiness.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers and other internal users do the safe thing by default with low-friction tools and workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter supports its claims with concrete technical examples, mechanisms, scope, or named artifacts rather than vague assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's backend engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains the practical outcomes or operational effects of the applicant's work, not just the activities performed.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Learning posture
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the applicant as coachable, collaborative, and ready to learn from security specialists.

levels.descriptor: Shows no sign of wanting to grow through security collaboration.
Shows indirect openness to learning or collaboration.
Explicitly emphasizes learning from security engineers or deepening security craft on the job.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures how coherent, memorable, and well-structured the letter's overall story and voice are, beyond a checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary product engineering, especially through CTFs or similar hands-on exercises.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through upstream contribution, maintenance, releases, reviews, or support for external users and contributors.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or one-off fixes to dependencies.
Describes regular contribution or maintenance responsibility.
Shows stewardship of an actively used project or community, including review and release responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed engineering work outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth and breadth of the applicant's directly relevant professional experience shipping, maintaining, operating, and owning production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantively the letter establishes Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Reliability and maintainability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes rigor, operability, maintainability, testing, and long-term system care as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific mission fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter understands this exact role's security-automation mission and maps the applicant's motivation and background to it.

levels.descriptor: Interest in the role is generic and could fit many software jobs.
The letter shows some interest in security or backend impact, but the motivation stays broad.
The letter clearly wants to make secure behavior easier by default or reduce repetitive security toil.
The letter offers a nuanced philosophy of security automation as leverage, capacity creation, or quiet resilience.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through methods like threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or fix validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the strength of formal third-party security certifications or other explicit external validation of security skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: System ownership
features.description: Captures how directly the letter presents the applicant as the person with autonomy and end-to-end responsibility for the systems described.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, prioritization, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface-level mechanical quality of the letter, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures genuinely idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to any broader recurring construct in the set.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
